description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved Indian dish featuring tender chicken simmered in a rich, creamy tomato-based sauce. This iconic curry offers a perfect balance of tangy, sweet, and mildly spicy flavors, making it a true comfort food. Our recipe guides you to create an authentic and restaurant-quality Butter Chicken right in your own kitchen.

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 15 minutes

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, Kashmiri red chili powder, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, turmeric powder, and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken thoroughly. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours.

instructions.title: Sear the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in batches, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Sear until browned on all sides and lightly cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove the chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add another 1 tablespoon of butter. Add the finely chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon of ginger garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Gravy
instructions.text: Add the crushed tomatoes, soaked cashews (drained), sugar, and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon of garam masala to the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Blend and Finish the Sauce
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. If needed, add a splash of water to achieve desired consistency. Pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an extra silky texture. This step ensures no cashew bits remain.

instructions.title: Combine Chicken and Sauce
instructions.text: Return the seared chicken to the smooth tomato sauce. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter and the crushed fenugreek leaves (Kasuri Methi). Stir well and simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to cook through completely and absorb the rich flavors of the sauce.

instructions.title: Add Cream and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the pan from heat and stir in the heavy cream. Mix gently until fully incorporated. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve hot with naan bread, basmati rice, or roti.

tips: For extra tender chicken, marinate overnight. The longer the marination, the more flavor the chicken absorbs.
Do not skip blending and sieving the sauce; it is key to achieving that signature smooth, restaurant-style consistency.
Always add heavy cream at the very end and off the heat to prevent it from splitting, ensuring a lusciously smooth finish.
article:
Savor the Flavors of India: Mastering Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani for Your Lunch

There are few dishes that evoke the rich, comforting essence of Indian cuisine quite like Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani. This iconic curry, celebrated worldwide for its velvety texture, sweet and tangy tomato-based sauce, and succulent pieces of marinated chicken, is a staple on restaurant menus and a beloved homemade treat. While it might seem like a complex dish reserved for special occasions, mastering Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani for your lunch is surprisingly achievable, and incredibly rewarding. Imagine the aroma filling your kitchen as you prepare this culinary masterpiece, promising a lunch that's anything but ordinary. Perfect for meal prep or a weekend cooking project, this recipe brings the heart of India right to your table.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

Butter Chicken, known in Hindi as Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Originating in Delhi, India, in the 1950s, this dish was created by Kundan Lal Jaggi and Kundan Lal Gujral, founders of the Moti Mahal restaurant. Legend has it that they sought a way to use leftover tandoori chicken, and thus, the rich, creamy tomato gravy was born. The genius of Murgh Makhani lies in its balance: the slight char and smokiness of the tandoor-cooked (or pan-fried) chicken is enveloped in a luxurious sauce made from tomatoes, cream, butter, and a delicate blend of aromatic spices. It's a dish that warms the soul, offers a symphony of flavors – sweet, savory, a touch of tang, and mild spice – and leaves you feeling utterly satisfied. Despite its indulgent name, a well-made Butter Chicken isn't overly heavy, making it a fantastic choice for a hearty and flavorful lunch.

## Ingredients You Need

To embark on your Butter Chicken journey, gather these essential ingredients. Quality matters here, especially for the tomatoes and cream, as they form the backbone of your sauce.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain full-fat yogurt
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 tsp red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for vibrant color)
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1/2 tsp garam masala
*   Salt to taste

For the Murgh Makhani Sauce:
*   2 tbsp unsalted butter (or ghee)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 tsp red chili powder
*   1 tsp ground cumin
*   1 tsp ground coriander
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1/2 tsp garam masala
*   1 (800g) can crushed tomatoes or 4-5 ripe fresh tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup cashew nuts, soaked in warm water for 15 minutes (for creaminess)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (or half-and-half for a lighter version)
*   1 tbsp kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1 tsp sugar (or to taste, to balance acidity)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps to create your own delectable Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring each piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, for maximum flavor.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add a little oil. Once hot, add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary, to avoid overcrowding the pan. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side. Set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In the same pan (or a clean pot), melt the butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
4.  **Add Aromatics and Spices:** Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant. Add the red chili powder, ground cumin, ground coriander, turmeric powder, and garam masala. Sauté for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, until aromatic.
5.  **Build the Tomato Base:** Pour in the crushed tomatoes (or fresh tomato puree). Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the raw tomato flavor mellows.
6.  **Create the Creamy Texture:** While the sauce simmers, drain the soaked cashews and blend them with a few tablespoons of water until you get a smooth paste. Stir this cashew paste into the tomato sauce.
7.  **Blend (Optional but Recommended):** For an incredibly smooth, restaurant-quality sauce, carefully transfer the sauce to a blender and blend until completely smooth. Alternatively, use an immersion blender directly in the pot. Return the blended sauce to the pot.
8.  **Finish the Sauce:** Stir in the heavy cream, kasuri methi, sugar, and salt to taste. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.
9.  **Combine and Serve:** Add the cooked chicken pieces to the sauce. Let it simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the rich sauce. Garnish generously with fresh cilantro.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that authentic, restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home is all about attention to detail.

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marinating time. The yogurt tenderizes the chicken, and the spices infuse it with flavor, preventing bland chicken in your rich sauce. Overnight marination yields the best results.
*   **Char the Chicken:** If possible, lightly char your chicken pieces, either in a hot pan or under a broiler. This adds a smoky depth that mimics the tandoor and is characteristic of true Murgh Makhani.
*   **Don't Rush the Sauce:** Allow the tomatoes to cook down thoroughly. This step is crucial for developing a deep, sweet flavor and eliminating any raw, acidic taste.
*   **Blend for Smoothness:** For that ultra-creamy, velvety texture, blending the sauce is non-negotiable. An immersion blender makes this step easy.
*   **Balance the Flavors:** Taste your sauce before serving. A good Butter Chicken has a delicate balance of sweet, tangy, and savory. Adjust sugar, salt, or a pinch of lemon juice if needed.
*   **Kasuri Methi Magic:** Don't skip the kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves). Crush them between your palms before adding; this releases their unique, slightly bitter, aromatic flavor that is essential to the dish.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a complete meal in itself, but it truly shines when paired with the right accompaniments. For a classic Indian lunch experience, serve it alongside warm, fluffy naan bread, perfect for scooping up every last drop of that incredible sauce. Steamed basmati rice is another excellent choice, absorbing the flavors beautifully. A cooling side of raita (yogurt with cucumber and mint) can offer a refreshing contrast, while a simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, and onion) adds a fresh crunch. Don't forget an extra sprinkle of fresh cilantro for presentation and a burst of herby flavor.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken is undeniably delicious, there are many ways to adapt this recipe to suit different tastes and dietary needs.

*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani:** Easily transform this dish into a vegetarian delight by substituting the chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), tofu, or even chickpeas. Simply pan-fry your chosen substitute until golden before adding it to the sauce.
*   **Vegan Version:** Replace the yogurt with a plant-based alternative like unsweetened coconut yogurt. Use plant-based butter or oil, and substitute heavy cream with full-fat coconut milk or cashew cream (made by blending soaked cashews with water).
*   **Spice Level:** If you prefer less heat, reduce the amount of red chili powder. For more heat, add a pinch of cayenne pepper or a chopped green chili to the sauce base.
*   **Healthier Options:** Use lean chicken breast, reduce the amount of butter and cream, or opt for half-and-half instead of heavy cream. The cashew paste still provides wonderful richness without excessive fat.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** To enhance the smoky depth, especially if you don't have a tandoor, try adding a drop of liquid smoke to the marinade or using smoked paprika.

Bringing the authentic taste of Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani into your home for lunch is a culinary adventure that promises rich rewards. From its humble origins to its global recognition, this dish continues to captivate palates with its creamy texture, vibrant flavors, and comforting warmth. With this detailed guide, you're now equipped to create a memorable Indian lunch that will impress and satisfy, proving that gourmet flavors can indeed be crafted right in your own kitchen. Enjoy the journey, and savor every delicious bite!
